body.p: REMARKS
Status of Claims
Claims 1-20 stand rejected.
Claims 1, 3, 5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14and 18 are currently amended.
Claim 2 is hereby canceled.
Claim 21 has been added.
Thus, claims 1 and 3-21 are now pending in this patent application.
The Applicant hereby requests further examination and reconsideration of the presently claimed application.
Drawing Objection

In the drawings, FIG. 5 is objected to because it lacks reference numeral "1" referred to in the Specification. A Replacement Sheet is submitted herewith amending FIG. 5 to show reference numeral "1" in conformance with the Specification. Withdrawal of the objection is respectfully requested.

Claims 13 and 14 are rejected as failing to comply with the written description requirement. Because the terms "electrocardiogram system" and "photoplethysmography system" do not appear in the specification. The terms have been amended to read "electrocardiogram module" and "photoplethysmography module" as disclosed in the Specification. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S. C. Q 112(b)

Claims 2, 5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, regards as the invention. Specifically, regarding claim 2, the limitation, "wherein the

screen further comprises a first side, wherein a groove is further disposed on the first side, and wherein the first electrode is disposed along the groove" is said to be unclear in light of the claim 1 limitation "a first electrode coupled to the screen so that the first electrode does not shield the display region, wherein the first electrode comprises a first surface... the first surface and the second surface are configured to contact a human body of a wearer". Claim 1 has been amended to clarify the position of the groove and fist electrode and claim 2 has been canceled. Claims 5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 18 depend from amended claim 1. Withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.

Regarding claims 2, 11, and 18, the claims recited "wherein the screen further comprises a first side, wherein a groove is further disposed on the first side" (Claim 2); "further comprising a first side configured to contact a wearer, wherein the housing comprises a bottom housing that is located on the firsts ide" (Claim 11); and "wherein the first side further comprises an edge..." (Claim 18), The office action asserted that these recitations were unclear. As noted above, claims 2 has been canceled. Claims 11 and 18 have been amended to clarify the locations of the bottom housing recited in claim 11 and the and edge recited in claim 18. Withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.

Regarding claims 5-6 and 10-11, the claims recited "wherein the screen further comprises a third surface facing away from the circuit board, wherein the groove is disposed in the third surface" (Claim 5); "wherein the screen further comprises a second side facing away from the third surface" (Claim 6); "wherein the housing comprises a third surface facing away from the screen, and wherein the second electrode is disposed on the third surface" (Claim 10); and "wherein the housing comprises a bottom housing that is located on the first side and wherein the third surface is on the bottom housing". The Office Action asserted that it was unclear whether the third surface in claims 5 and 6 is the same as or different from the third surface in claims 10 and 11 Claims 5 and 6 have

been amended to clarify the location of the first electrode. Claims 10 and 11 have been amended to clarify the location of the second electrode. Withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.

Regarding claims 13 and 14, the claims recited "further comprising an electrocardiogram system electrically coupled to the first electrode and the second electrode by the circuit board" (Claim 13) and "further comprising a photoplethysmography system mounted on the housing and configured to detect a heart rate of the human body" (Claim 14).The Office Action asserted that it is unclear what structural components may be incorporated or excluded from the electrocardiogram system (i.e. module) and the photoplethysmography system (i.e. module) to perform the claimed function, and that one of ordinary skill in the art would not be appraised of the metes and bounds of the claim scope given the specification and that claims 13 an4 14 are therefore rendered indefinite. Claims 13 and 14 have been amended to recite "electrocardiogram module" and "photoplethysmography module" as described in the Specification. Withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. Q 102

Claims 1, 2, 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Chinese Patent CN 107865653A ("Jiang"). Claim 1 is independent. Claim 2 has been canceled. Claims 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18 depend from independent claim 1. Therefore, claims 1, 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18 will be allowable over Jiang if independent claim 1 is allowable over Jiang. According to MPEP § 2131, "[a] claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." The Applicant respectfully asserts that Jiang fails to teach each and every element of independent claim 1, and consequently also fails to anticipate dependent claims 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18. With regard to independent claim 1, Jiang fails to disclose a connecting section, a
groove disposed on the connecting section and on a portion of the display region, and a first electrode
disposed in the groove. Claim 1 has been amended and now reads:
1. A wearable device comprising:
a housing;
a circuit board disposed within the housing;
a screen comprising:
a display region;
a connecting section;
a groove disposed on the connecting section and on a portion of the
display region;
a first electrode disposed in the groove and coupled to the screen, wherein
the first electrode comprises a first surface; and
a second electrode mounted on the housing, wherein the second electrode
comprises a second surface,
wherein the first electrode and the second electrode are electrically coupled
by the circuit board, and
wherein the first surface and the second surface are configured to contact a
human body of a wearer.
(Emphasis added). As shown, Claim 1 requires a connecting section, a groove disposed on the
connecting section and on a portion of the display region, and a first electrode disposed in the
groove. The amendment is supported by the disclosure, e.g. claim 2, FIGS. 1-4 and paragraphs
0056-0057. As noted above, claim 2 has been canceled and the groove is now recited in claim 1.
The Office Action (at page 10) asseverates that Figure 3 of Jiang discloses a groove and that "[i]t
would be obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art to include the first electrode (i.e. P2) within
the groove.

The Applicant respectfully disagrees. Firstly, the 35 U.S.C. § 102 rejection requires each and every element as set forth in the claim to be found, either expressly or inherently described in the reference. The assertion in the Office Action that the relationship between the first electrode and the groove would be obvious is not only misplaced, but it underscores the fact that the reference does not explicitly or inherently disclose a groove disposed on the connecting section and on a portion of the display region, and a first electrode disposed in the groove. Secondly, Jiang does not in fact disclose or even suggest a groove. A carefull reading of Jiang reveals no "groove', synonyms of groove, or illustration or discussion that could easonable interpreted to disclose a groove as claimed. The label "groove" was added to Figure 3 of Jiang, apparently for the purpose of making the rejection. In effect, the Office Action, perhaps inadvertently, invented prior art. The Applicant respectfully asserts that because Jiang fails to teach each and every element of independent claim 1, it consequently also fails to anticipate dependent claims 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18, and that the rejections must be withdrawn. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. Q 103

Claims 3 and 4 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Jiang in view of Korean Patent Application Publication KR 2007/0080330A ("Song"). Claims 5 and 6 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Jiang in view of US Patent 10729347 ("Schleicher"). Claims 7-9, 12 and 14-16 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Jiang in view of US Patent Application Publication 2019/0072912 ("Pandya"). Claim 19 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Jiang in view of Song and further in view of US Patent Application Publication 2009/0294765 ("Tanaka"). Claim 20 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Jiange in view of Schelicher and further in view of US Patent Application Publication 2013/0281814 ("Tilt"). The United States Supreme Court in Graham v. John Deere Co. of Kansas City noted that an obviousness determination begins with a finding that

"the prior art as a whole in one form or another contains all" of the elements of the claimed invention. See Graham v. John Deere Co. of Kansas City, 383 U.S. 1, 22 (U.S. 1966). The secondary references Song, Schleicher, Pandya, Tanaka and Tilt do not teach the claim elements missing from Jiang.

With further regard to claim 6, rejected as being unpatentable over Jiang in view Schleicher, the Applicant respectfully asserts that Schleicher fails to disclose that the first electrode further comprises a first main body part disposed in the groove, a second main body part configured to electrically couple to the circuit board, and a connecting section coupled to the first main body part and the second main body part to electrically couple the first main body part and the second main body part. Claim 6 has been amended and now reads:
6. The wearable device of claim 5, wherein the first electrode further
comprises:
a first main body part disposed in the groove;
a second main body part configured to electrically couple to the circuit
board; and
a connecting section coupled to the first main body part and the second main
body part to electrically couple the first main body part and the second main body
part.
As detailed above, Jiang does not teach the groove. At pages 18-19 of the Office Action Schleicher is cited for allegedly teaching:

...the first electrode further comprises a first main body part disposed in the groove, a second main body part disposed on the second side and configured to electrically couple to the circuit board; and a connecting section coupled to the first main body part and the second main body part to electrically couple the first main body part and
the second main body part. (See annotated FIG. 2 below.

It is respectfully submitted that there is no teaching in FIG. 2 or elsewhere in Schleicher that would make it obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before to modify the wearable device of Jiang to arrive at the configuration recited in claim 6 to include a first main body part disposed in the groove, a second main body part configured to electrically couple to the circuit board, and a connecting section coupled to the first main body part and the second main body part to electrically couple the first main body part and the second main body part. For this additional reason, the rejection of claim
6 should be withdrawn.
New Claim

New claim 21 recites novel and non-obvious aspects ofthe disclosure. Support for new claim 21 is found in at least previously presented claim 5 of the application. Thus, no new matter is contained in this claim. Claim 21 depends from claim 1, which is allowable for the reasons stated above. Thus, claim 21 is also allowable on at least the same grounds as its base claim.

Consideration of the foregoing amendments and remarks, reconsideration of the application, and withdrawal of the rejections and objections is respectfully requested by the Applicant. No new matter is introduced by way of the amendment. It is believed that each ground of rejection raised in the Office Action dated August 27, 2024 has been fully addressed.
